content: Aluminium iodide refers to any chemical compound that consists solely of aluminium and iodine. Typically, the term aluminium iodide is used to describe the compound with the chemical formula AlI₃. This compound is formed either through the direct reaction of aluminium metal with iodine or by the action of hydrogen iodide (HI) on aluminium metal. Similar to its related halides, aluminium chloride and aluminium bromide, AlI₃ is a strong Lewis acid and must be stored in conditions that protect it from exposure to the atmosphere. Applications in Organic Synthesis Aluminium iodide is utilized in organic synthesis to cleave specific types of chemical bonds, particularly carbon-oxygen (C-O) and nitrogen-oxygen (N-O) bonds. It is effective in breaking aryl ethers and in the deoxygenation of epoxides. Aluminium(I) Iodide The term aluminium iodide is most commonly associated with the triiodide form (AlI₃) or its dimer. However, aluminium monoiodide (AlI) also plays a role in the aluminium-iodine system. Despite this, AlI is thermodynamically unstable at room temperature and tends to decompose into the triiodide form. An example of a derivative of aluminium monoiodide is the cyclic adduct formed with triethylamine, which has the formula Al₄I₄(NEt₃)₄. Safety When aluminium triiodide undergoes hydrolysis, it releases hydrogen iodide (HI), a corrosive substance. Additionally, as a strong Lewis acid, aluminium iodide can act as a skin irritant and should be handled with appropriate safety precautions.
